- **NVFP4 B300 Dynamo+SGLang ([InferenceX #4346](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4346), in progress).** Same deployment shapes as before (agg TP8/TP4/DEP8, disagg 1P1D/1P2D DEP8). These files mirror the launches as submitted, and the variable is part of the submitted launches. It is not a no-op in every image that ran:
- In `v0.5.17-cu130` / `v0.5.18-cu130` (GLM-5.2 GB200 Dynamo+SGLang agg and disagg) it is a live switch (`EnvBool(False)`) that selects the unified radix cache, so dropping it would not run what SemiAnalysis measured.
- In the 2026-09 nightlies and `v0.5.19-cu130` it is deprecated, and in `dev-cu13-nightly-09242` it has no effect.

The regenerated data therefore has it again, on the same lanes as before #45090. #45090's edits outside the AgentX data (`environ.py` and the hand-written DeepSeek-V4 AMD commands) are untouched.

**Not mirrored:**
- `musespark-fp4-h100-sglang-agentic-dflash` and `qwen3.5-fp8-h100-sglang-agentic`: no dashboard changelog names a run for them (as in #45311).
- `qwen3.5-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-agg-pareto` and `-pp-pareto` are deleted by [InferenceX #4333](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4333) (as in #45311).

The pipeline is the same as in #45311, with these changes:

- **`--attn-dp-size`.** It is the non-deprecated spelling of `--dp-size N --enable-dp-attention` (#41818), first used by [InferenceX #4346](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4346). Deployment labels (`DEP8`), GPU counts and KV-donor matching now read it as DP attention.
- **Rules.** Kept as submitted: worker flags `--attn-dp-size`, `--enable-torch-symm-mem` and `--preferred-sampling-params`, and the Dynamo-only worker flags `--dyn-reasoning-parser` and `--dyn-tool-call-parser` (dropped from the derived SGLang-router variant, which keeps `--reasoning-parser`).

Each lane is still rendered at the exact commit of the run that produced its data, or at the PR head while in progress.
- **Removed (SA-only settings):** the benchmark harness, cluster paths and caches, telemetry, and InferenceX's synthetic speculative acceptance (disclosed per deployment).
- **Replaced with placeholders:** IPs, ports and NICs.
- **Derived variants:** router and KV-offload variants that were not run are derived and labeled "Derived — not run".

The data files are generated, so there is no hand-written code to review here.

  - `mint broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects`
  - `mint validate`
  - `pre-commit run --all-files` in `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13`

  - The copy buttons work on a plain-HTTP preview.
- **Decoder and KV flags.** The component's own decoder, run through Node, reproduces the Python-generated commands for all 2,698 combinations, including every point's measured tier. Every KV-cache flag in a shown command exists in the SGLang commit of its deployment's image.
- **Round trip and leak scan.** Every flag and variable of every submitted launch is kept, rewritten or removed by a rule, and no SemiAnalysis cluster artifact appears in the shown commands.
- **Diff against #45311's data.** The baseline is #45311's data; `main` differs from it only by #45090's deletion, covered above.

  | Page | Command sets |
  |---|---|
  | GLM-5.3 | 48 added ([InferenceX #3930](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3930)) |
  | GLM-5.2 | 340 identical |
  | DeepSeek-V4 | 282 identical; 42 changed ([InferenceX #4346](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/4346)); 34 derived-HiCache rows of the B300 single-node lanes changed (new donor) |
  | DeepSeek-V4.1 | 396 identical |
  | Qwen3.5 | 1,096 identical |
  | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 94 identical |
  | Muse Spark Open | 90 identical; 114 changed, 120 removed and 108 added (retunes); 54 added (new GB300 Dynamo+SGLang lane) |

- **Cluster environment.** The table matches the worker fingerprints of measured runs on every cluster with srt-slurm lanes.
- **Argument parsing.** 315 distinct `sglang.launch_server`, `dynamo.sglang`, `sglang_router.launch_router` and `dynamo.frontend` command lines are new since #45311. All parse in their own submission images:
  - `dev-muse-spark-open@sha256:8cfc5a72…` 203/203;
  - `nightly-dev-20261019-3c560089` 60/60;
  - `nightly-dev-efa-20261019-3c560089` 39/39;
  - `v0.5.20-cu130@sha256:b27fce60…` 13/13.

  Each nightly's amd64 and arm64 builds come from the same SGLang commit (`3c560089`). The other 2,070 of the 2,385 command lines are identical to ones parsed for earlier cookbook PRs. Environment variables are not part of this check.

No serving or benchmark runs were performed for this PR; the numbers live in the linked SemiAnalysis runs. SGLang CI was not triggered.

+## Agentic Long-Context Deployment
+
+Agentic workloads, such as coding agents and other multi-turn, tool-using assistants, send long prompts whose prefixes grow and repeat from turn to turn. Serving them well depends on reusing the KV cache across turns, offloading it beyond GPU memory, and keeping each session on the workers that already hold its prefix. This section gives complete launch commands for such deployments, each benchmarked in [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) and linked to the run that measured it. Pick a hardware platform, checkpoint, deployment shape, concurrency, KV cache offloading mechanism and router to get every process of the deployment as a raw command, one tab per process in launch order.
+
+- **Router.** Each configuration was submitted behind one front door: Dynamo (`dynamo.frontend` with `dynamo.sglang` workers) or SGLang (`sglang.launch_server`, behind `sglang_router` when there are several workers or DP-attention ranks).
+- **KV offload.** Choose among these KV cache offloading mechanisms: none (GPU KV only), HiCache (host DRAM), or a Mooncake store attached through the external linker. The Mooncake option needs an image whose SGLang build includes `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker`.

 ## 1. Model Introduction
 
 **GLM-5.3** is Z.ai's flagship Mixture-of-Experts model built on **DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA)**: a lightning indexer selects a sparse set of key tokens per query (top-2048), so attention cost stays near-constant as context grows. It keeps the same base architecture while updating post-training for complex coding and long-horizon tasks. It ships in two precisions — **FP8** (`zai-org/GLM-5.3`) and full **BF16** (`zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16`) — both with **78 transformer layers**, **256 routed experts** (8 active per token), a **1M-token context window**, and a single **MTP (Multi-Token Prediction)** layer for built-in EAGLE-style speculative decoding. FP8 is the recommended deployment; BF16 (~1.5 TB) needs an 8×B300 node or a multi-node setup. For Blackwell, RadixArk publishes an **experimental NVFP4** build (`RadixArk/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`, Model Optimizer) that quantizes only the routed experts' linear weights and activations to 4-bit (attention, shared experts, dense layers, MTP, embeddings, and the LM head stay unquantized), cutting the weight footprint to ~0.45 TB so a 4-GPU GB300 node can serve it with TP4. **The NVFP4 cells are experimental** — benchmark data (accuracy / throughput) is still pending; treat them as provisional until the benchmark cards fill in.
